title: Quantum detection of CP violation in the $t\bar{t}$ system: production
authors: Priyanka Lamba, Fabio Maltoni, Olimpia Miniati, Eleni Vryonidou
abstract: We investigate how possible new CP-violating top-quark interactions are encoded in the quantum state of a produced $t\bar t$ pair. We derive analytic expressions for the production density matrix in several benchmark channels relevant to hadron, lepton and photon colliders. In a common spin basis, we identify two characteristic CP-odd structures in the Fano--Bloch decomposition: a difference between the top and antitop polarisation vectors and an antisymmetric component of the spin-correlation matrix. We construct observables that directly probe these structures and study how quantum information measures, including discord, concurrence, magic and trace distance, respond to CP-even and CP-odd SMEFT contributions. Finally, using current measurements and future collider projections, we assess the sensitivity of these observables to possible new sources of CP violation in top-quark production. This establishes the production-level framework whose experimental reconstruction is developed in a companion paper.
summary: This paper develops a theoretical framework to search for CP violation in top-quark pair production by analyzing the spin polarization and correlations of the produced $t ar{t}$ state. It uses advanced tools from quantum information theory, such as discord and concurrence, applied to the density matrix derived from SMEFT extensions. The work provides a clean, model-independent diagnostic tool for future collider experiments.
main_problem: To investigate how potential new CP-violating top-quark interactions are encoded within the quantum state of a produced $t ar{t}$ pair and to identify suitable quantum observables sensitive to this violation.
main_result: The paper establishes a production-level framework using quantum information measures (like discord and concurrence) that directly probe CP-odd structures in the $t ar{t}$ spin density matrix, independent of decay kinematics.
method: Analytic derivation of the $t ar{t}$ spin density matrix using SMEFT operators, followed by constructing observables based on quantum information theory applied to the state's polarization and correlations.
model_or_system: The system is the production of a top-antitop pair ($t ar{t}$) via various hard scattering processes ($	ext{e}^+	ext{e}^-, \gamma\gamma, q ar{q}, gg$). The theoretical framework incorporates potential new physics through dimension-six SMEFT operators.
key_observables: Polarisation asymmetries, the difference between top and antitop polarisation vectors, the anti-symmetric component of the spin-correlation matrix, quantum information measures (discord, concurrence, magic, trace distance).
important_parameters: The new physics scale ($\Lambda$) and the Wilson coefficients ($C_i$) associated with CP-violating SMEFT operators.
main_assumptions: The analysis focuses strictly on the production state density matrix; reconstruction from decay products is deferred to a companion paper. Tree-level calculations are used, neglecting absorptive phases.
figures_summary: Not specified in the notes, but the structure suggests comparisons across different collider channels and sensitivity plots for various observables.
paper_structure: The paper systematically introduces CP-violating SMEFT interactions, derives the production density matrix in a common spin basis, identifies characteristic CP-odd structures, constructs corresponding observables, and finally assesses their sensitivity using quantum information measures.
why_interesting: While focused on particle physics, the methodology—mapping fundamental symmetries (CP) onto quantifiable quantum state properties (discord, concurrence)—is directly transferable to analyzing coherence loss or symmetry breaking in complex many-body quantum systems.
